result.reason: I kept 4 findings: 3 important, all untested new behavior, and 1 nit. I dropped 4 candidates.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: The new openingChangeWithin() gives either an "opens" or a "closes" change, and the warning text quotes it. No test checks the "opens" case. No test calls openingChangeWithin() directly. No test checks a change after midnight, which clockText() writes as "the next day". The only test that covers this text is Milt's "closes at 12:30 p.m.".
findings.failure_case: Say a bug drops the "opens" entries, or always reports "closes". Then a museum that opens at 11:00 a.m., visited from 10:00 a.m., would get the wrong opening time in its warning. Every test would still pass, because Milt's only closes during its visit.
findings.label_reason: This change adds the opening/closing text, and no test would fail if the "opens" path were removed or wrong. So it's F6. It's not F1, because a run shows the code gives the right answer: { change: 'opens', minute: 1020 } for a 4 p.m. visit to a bar that opens at 5 p.m.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: drivingResult() warns when a day drives more than the hours its approval gives, even when that's within the comfortable hours. That's the `!isOver && approved !== null && !isApproved` path. Every driving test uses a day that's over the comfortable hours. So nothing checks this path.
findings.failure_case: Say the condition were simplified to `if (!isOver) return null`. Then a day approved for 3 hours that drives 3 h 30 m, with 4 comfortable hours, would give no warning. Every test would still pass.
findings.label_reason: This change adds the rule, and deleting it breaks no test, so it's F6. The code itself does what its comment says, so none of the labels above F6 fit.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: misfitOf() has a branch that warns about a nearEndPlace stop on a day that's not the last day. The search area test covers only a stop near a stay and a stop near the start place. No test checks the end-place branch or its text, "the end place, but it's no longer on the last day".
findings.failure_case: Say the `day !== itinerary.lastDay` branch were deleted or inverted. Then a pie stop near Mike's house, moved to Day 2 of 5, would give no warning. No test would fail.
findings.label_reason: This change adds the check, and no test would catch it being removed, so it's F6. I found no wrong behavior in the branch, so the labels above F6 don't fit.

findings.label: N1
findings.problem: openingHoursText() falls back to "is open for only X of the visit" when openingChangeWithin() returns null. That can't happen. This text is used only when the open minutes are more than 0 and fewer than the visit's length. In that case some opening or closing always falls strictly inside the visit. So the fallback is code that never runs.
findings.failure_case: No input reaches the fallback text. A visit that's partly open always has a boundary inside it, so `change` is never null when `open > 0`.
findings.label_reason: This is code that never runs, which the rubric lists under N1. The change added it, so it's a nit.

dropped.problem: The driving text "You agreed to 5." gives the approved hours without a unit, which could be unclear to the coordinator.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: Domain model section 4.8 gives this exact text, "Day 4 needs about 5 h 20 m of driving. You agreed to 5.". The code matches it, and the sentence before it gives the unit (h/m). So the text isn't false, and an agent wouldn't misread it.

dropped.problem: stopOrderResult() builds the day's own order from all stops that have a place. If Google's best order left some of those stops out, the two lists would differ, and a false stop-order note would follow.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: LegsService.#stopOrderOf builds stopsInBestOrder from route.stops, which holds the same stops that have a place. Waypoints are kept apart. And when Google's order is the same as the day's, timeSavedInMinutes is 0, so the `Math.max(1, ...)` guard refuses the note anyway.

dropped.problem: isOpeningHoursApprovalApplying() reads only stop.approvals[0]. A stop with more than one opening-hours approval could be judged on an old one.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: withApproval() in approval.ts replaces any approval of the same kind, and checkedApprovals() refuses two of a kind. A stop holds only opening-hours approvals, so there's at most one.

dropped.problem: openingChangeWithin() could get the weekday wrong for an overnight visit or a period that runs across the week's end.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: A run of the code shows it works. A Monday 5 p.m. to 2 a.m. bar, visited from 11 p.m. to 3 a.m., gives closes at minute 1560, which reads "2:00 a.m. the next day", with 180 open minutes. A Saturday visit against a Sunday-only period gives 0 open minutes and no change.
